themes.consensus_view: All three desks treat the AI buildout as the dominant corporate spending story right now, but they split on whether that spending pays for itself, with Deutsche Bank pointing to Meta funding it from a strong core business and The Market Ear asking whether AI revenue arrives fast enough to cover the cost of the money being spent.

themes.consensus_view: The banks agree the violent forced selling in AI and chip names was traders being flushed out of crowded bets rather than the business story breaking, leaving the group much less crowded now, but they disagree on whether that makes AI the trade to buy back or the money source funding a move into the rest of the market.

facts_agreed.claim: The forced unwind has left investors far less crowded into the AI complex than they were at the peak, so positioning is no longer the main thing hanging over the sector.
evidence_quotes: positioning is no longer the overhang it was a week ago
positioning significantly cleaner than at the peak

facts_agreed.claim: The chip-sector selloff was driven by investors being forced out of crowded positions, not by the underlying businesses getting worse.
evidence_quotes: recent semiconductor sell-off has been driven more by positioning than deteriorating fundamentals

facts_agreed.claim: Money leaving the AI trade is spreading into the rest of the market, but only into names with holding-up earnings rather than everything indiscriminately.
